title: Two Travelers and One Flask
text:
The Talmud records a hard case that the sages argued about. Two people are walking through the desert, far from any town. Only one of them has a flask of water. If both of them drink from it, both will die before they reach a settlement. If only one drinks, that one will reach a settlement alive.

The sage Ben Petura taught that it is better for both to drink and die, so that neither should have to watch the death of his companion. The water should be shared, whatever it costs.

Then Rabbi Akiva came and taught differently. He pointed to a verse in Leviticus about helping a brother in need: "that your brother may live with you." With you, Akiva said, means that your own life comes first. The one who owns the water should drink it.

The Talmud gives Akiva's view as the conclusion, and the passage has been studied and argued over ever since.
lesson: Caring for others does not require you to destroy yourself. Look after your own life so that you can go on helping, and take hard dilemmas seriously instead of pretending they are easy.
